title: API gateway: tier-aware rate limiting + standardized 429 reason codes/headers
creator: Ethan Park
description: Implement tier-aware rate limiting at the API gateway for protected hot routes (chat/completions, embeddings, rerank). Enforce consistent 429 semantics across Hosted API + Dedicated front doors, including reason codes and standardized headers. Must be low overhead on critical path and deterministic/auditable for enterprise escalations. Non-goal: billing changes (only metadata hooks).
content:
Background / why
- We’ve had multiple incidents where a small number of high-traffic workloads push shared pools into tail-latency + 5xx cascades. The gateway is the earliest consistent enforcement point we control across hosted/dedicated front doors.
- We need predictable overload behavior: enterprise traffic should preserve SLOs longer, best-effort should be throttled earlier, and customers/support need clear signals in 429 responses.

Scope
1) Tier-aware rate limiter
- Evaluate limits based on: (tenant/org), tier (enterprise vs best-effort/self-serve), route group (protected route groups), and region.
- Support both:
  a) fixed-window quota checks (longer windows; often configured via quotas service)
  b) short-window rate limiter (per-second/minute shaping at gateway)
- Ensure low-cardinality keying and local caching for policy lookup results.

2) Standardized 429 semantics (payload + headers)
- All gateway 429 responses MUST include reason code + retry guidance.
- Align on a single set of headers with stable names so SDKs + customer code can implement consistent backoff.

3) Observability / supportability
- Emit gateway metrics for 429 outcomes with bounded cardinality (route_group not raw path, tier not account ID).
- Ensure we can correlate a customer-reported 429 with the exact reason category without requiring deep on-call access.

Acceptance criteria
- Tier routing rules applied at gateway for route groups: chat_completions, embeddings, rerank (MVP).
- Enterprise tier receives distinct budgets/limits vs best-effort; best-effort is throttled earlier during pressure.
- 429 responses are consistent across all protected routes with:
  - reason code (machine readable)
  - message (human readable)
  - stable headers (see below)
- P95 added gateway latency for policy+limit evaluation <= 1.0ms (measured in canary), and no >1% regression in gateway CPU.
- Metrics present and dashboards can compute 429 rate by tier + route_group + reason.

Design details
A) Policy evaluation contract
- Gateway queries policy engine (ENG-4923) for an allow/deny decision and (if deny) a denial reason + retry hint. Gateway remains the enforcement point.
- To avoid high overhead:
  - Cache policy results locally by (org_id, route_group, tier) with short TTL (target 30s; configurable).
  - Batch lookups for concurrent requests on the same key when the cache is cold.

B) Limits model (gateway)
- Rate limit: token bucket (or leaky bucket) for short windows.
- Quota: fixed window counters with external evaluation (existing quotas path), but normalized error semantics.

C) 429 reason codes (gateway output)
- error.code (string):
  - rate_limit_exceeded: gateway token-bucket rate limit hit
  - quota_exceeded: quota window exceeded (daily/hourly)
  - overload_shed: request rejected due to fleet pressure/admission control signal (best-effort first)
  - route_budget_exhausted: protected route budget consumed for tier (typically best-effort)
  - policy_denied: policy engine deny for tier/route (catch-all; should be rare)

Notes:
- We explicitly separate quota vs overload so Support can answer “you are over your purchased allowance” vs “temporary fleet protection.”
- If a request is denied by policy engine but without a specific reason, default to policy_denied.

D) Standard 429 response body
- JSON response uses existing Redwood error envelope shape to match SDK parsing:
  - error.type = "rate_limit_error"
  - error.code = one of the reason codes above
  - error.message = short actionable message
  - error.param = null
  - error.request_id = request id string

E) Standard 429 headers
- Always present:
  - Retry-After: integer seconds (best effort; may be 0 for immediate retry with jitter)
  - X-Request-Id: pass-through
  - X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reason: same value as error.code
  - X-Redwood-Tier: enterprise|best_effort (as evaluated)
  - X-Redwood-Route-Group: chat_completions|embeddings|rerank|other
- When rate-limited (rate_limit_exceeded):
  - X-RateLimit-Limit: integer (requests per window)
  - X-RateLimit-Remaining: integer
  - X-RateLimit-Reset: unix seconds
- When quota-limited (quota_exceeded):
  - X-Redwood-Quota-Limit: integer (requests or units)
  - X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining: integer
  - X-Redwood-Quota-Reset: unix seconds

F) Config + rollout
- Feature flags (ENG-4928):
  - hot_route_protection.gateway_tier_limits_enabled
  - hot_route_protection.gateway_429_standard_enabled
- Allowlist support by org_id for canary, and independent per-region enablement.

Observability
- Metrics (names aligned with observability standards doc):
  - gateway_requests_total{route_group,tier,outcome}
  - gateway_rate_limited_total{route_group,tier,reason}
  - gateway_rate_limit_eval_latency_ms{route_group}
- Cardinality rules:
  - NO raw path labels.
  - NO org_id/customer_id tags.
  - route_group is a small enum.

Rollout plan
1) Merge behind flags, no behavior change by default.
2) us-east canary: allowlist 3–5 enterprise orgs + shadow mode metrics only for 24h.
3) Enable enforcement for best_effort tier on protected routes (enterprise remains permissive) and monitor.
4) Enable enterprise tier limits with conservative budgets and monitor SLO dashboards.
5) Expand to eu-west + remaining regions.

Links
- Confluence ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-hot-route-capacity-protection-enforcement-points.json
- Tech design: sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/hot-route-capacity-protection-technical-design.json
- Support doc for reason codes: sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/enterprise-priority-429-and-quota-behavior.json
- GitHub PR (gateway): sources/github/redwood/pr-27411-add-tier-aware-rate-limiter-to-api-gateway.json
- GitHub PR (reason codes follow-up): sources/github/redwood/pr-27441-add-overload-reason-codes-to-429-responses.json

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: added latency on critical path.
  - Mitigation: local cache + fast path; measure and gate rollout on canary.
- Risk: inconsistent behavior between gateway and downstream routing admission control.
  - Mitigation: keep reason codes aligned; gateway uses policy engine denial reasons where possible.
- Risk: customer confusion (“why am I getting 429s now?”).
  - Mitigation: stable headers + docs + Support macros; clear reason separation quota vs overload.

Out of scope
- Billing changes or dynamic pricing. (We only emit reason metadata; billing remains as-is.)
- Full fairness scheduling rewrite.
comments: 2025-12-02 (Ethan Park): Marking P0 given incident follow-ups. Need gateway-level semantics nailed before we can do customer comms. Please coordinate with Jordan (policy engine) on denial contract.

2025-12-05 (Amara Diallo): Drafted header spec proposal. Question: should we reuse X-RateLimit-* vs Redwood-specific for quota? Proposal: use X-RateLimit-* only for short-window limiter; use X-Redwood-Quota-* for quotas to avoid misleading semantics.

2025-12-07 (Jordan Lee): +1 on separating quota vs rate limit. Policy engine can return denial reason as enum; gateway should map 1:1 to X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reason to avoid drift. Will add to ENG-4923 schema.
2025-12-10 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure 429 reason label is bounded. We got burned by high-cardinality tags last quarter. route_group is OK; do not add customer identifiers.

2025-12-14 (Nikhil Sharma): Product request: keep customer-facing message neutral (“capacity protection active”)—avoid calling it “enterprise priority” in the message. Reason code can still reflect overload_shed.

2025-12-18 (Amara Diallo): Implemented tier evaluation hook based on auth context + org plan. Added local cache for (org_id, route_group, tier) policy lookups (TTL 30s). Added metrics for eval latency.

2026-01-03 (Sergio Costa): Tested dashboard queries against gateway metrics in staging; looks good. Need to ensure outcome/deny counters include route_group mapping for /v1/chat/completions vs legacy chat routes.
2026-01-08 (Amara Diallo): Canary in us-east enabled for allowlisted orgs. Observed p95 policy eval 0.42ms, no meaningful gateway CPU increase. 429s match expected headers; Retry-After present.

2026-01-11 (Owen Phillips): Support request: ensure X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reason always present even when older clients hit legacy throttle path. Otherwise it’s hard to triage tickets. Please confirm legacy path removed or mapped.

2026-01-16 (Amara Diallo): Follow-up PR adds overload_shed + route_budget_exhausted mapping and forces reason header on all 429 emitted by gateway. Also added integration tests to cover missing header regressions.
2026-01-24 (Ethan Park): Marking Done. GA headers/semantics merged and rolled out behind flags. Remaining work tracked in ENG-4930 (Support macros) + ENG-4927 (incident-bot notifications).
